CarTrade Tech (CARTRADE) · The story so far From a small car site to India's biggest used-goods marketplace, and the bet to earn more from the same users. How it got here • 2010: started as CarTrade, an online car marketplace • 2016: bought CarWale and BikeWale, the car and bike research sites • 2018: bought 51% of Shriram Automall, which auctions vehicles for banks and lenders • 2021: listed on the stock market • Aug 2023: bought OLX India for ₹523 Cr, shut the loss-making car-buying arm that came with it, and moved OLX onto its own tech in 3 months instead of 6 • FY24 to FY26: revenue went from ₹490 Cr to ₹779 Cr while costs grew far slower, so margins rose from about 9% to over 30%. Without OLX, underlying growth was about 16% a year What it is today • CarWale/BikeWale: new-car research, paid about 70% by car makers and 30% by dealers • OLX India: used goods, with about 63% of used-car listing value • Shriram Automall: vehicle auctions (about 55% owned) • 92–100% of visitors arrive without paid ads The bet Earn more from the same users instead of buying new ones: charge OLX buyers for the first time (Elite Buyer), premium plans for sellers, verified listings, car loans with IDFC FIRST and a retail tie-up with Spinny. Management's targets: ₹1,000 Cr profit in 4–5 years (about 4x FY26) and a "40-40" goal (40% profit growth, margins above 40%). The record 3 of 4 financial promises met, 1 slip in 13 dated ones. The miss: OLX growth was meant to speed up in Q4 FY26 and didn't, because a product launched 45 days late. OLX then grew 29% in Q1 FY27, against a weak quarter a year earlier. What the documents also show • Growth is slowing: revenue +16% in Q1 FY27, from 19–25% through FY26. Consumer visitors +7%, auction volumes flat. Profit still rises because each user earns more • The edge is OLX's buyer–seller network, not brand or lock-in. Open risks: AI search taking CarWale's Google traffic, and Facebook Marketplace • Other income, mostly interest on ₹1,321 Cr of cash, is about 30% of pre-tax profit. The tax rate was 16% in FY26 and is heading to 23–24% (already near 24% in Q1 FY27). Return on equity is about 10%, which management agrees is below its cost of capital because of the cash • On our valuation check, today's price implies about 41% earnings growth a year over the next few years, above the broker forecasts we hold (about 25–37%) What to watch 1. Do OLX business buyers pay, or leave, as charging rolls out? 2. Can OLX hold 25%+ growth against normal comparisons? 3. Does the 31% Q1 margin keep rising through FY27, as management guides? 🆕 New coverage: Azad Engineering (AZAD) Azad makes precision turbine blades and engine parts in Hyderabad for GE Vernova, Siemens Energy, Mitsubishi Heavy and Baker Hughes, and for Rolls-Royce and Honeywell in aerospace. Exports were 93% of FY26 revenue. The story is capacity: eight plants, each built for one customer, to turn a ₹6,500 Cr order book into revenue. Four are open and four are due by March 2027. In July it also delivered India's first indigenous expendable turbojet engine to DRDO. What the first read found: • 9 of 12 closed financial guides met, but plant and programme dates slipped 12 times • Working capital stretched to 244 days in FY26 • The price implies about 60% a year earnings growth; management guides 25%-plus revenue growth Company page · Every promise, tracked · Industry The story in words: A workshop for every client, and nobody pays before the fitting

Jyoti CNC and Macpower CNC make the same machines in the same city. Macpower's own CMD says they share "a same product basket, same distribution network".

Jyoti has the better record on paper: revenue up 31% a year over three years against 18%, at a 25% margin against 16%. But over FY22-26 Jyoti turned ₹750 Cr of profit into minus ₹18 Cr of operating cash. Macpower turned ₹109 Cr into ₹36 Cr.

FY27: Jyoti's plant is full and its new block, re-dated three times, is due this week. Macpower is filling a plant it already owns.

The prices: Jyoti implies about 45% earnings growth a year, above our bull case of 31-38%. Macpower about 38%, at the top of our base case.

Which risk would you rather own: an oven not yet lit, or one that must run hotter?

🆕 New coverage: Bondada Engineering (BONDADA) A Hyderabad contractor that builds and maintains solar plants, battery storage and telecom networks. Renewables were 79% of FY26's ₹2,842.8 Cr revenue, up from 58% a year earlier, with a ₹7,147.5 Cr order book. The bet: grow from solar contractor into an owner of power assets, with 850 MWh of its own battery storage earning from Q1 FY28 and a 2 GW solar park, toward $1 bn of revenue by 2030. What decides it is build speed: 492 MWp commissioned in FY26, 1.5 GWp targeted for FY27. What the first read found: • Guides mostly missed: 1 of 4 closed financial guides met, though dates held (6 slips across 26 dated promises). • Cash is the weak spot: EPC margins are thin (EBITDA 11.5%) and profits have been slow to turn into cash. • Management guides 60-70% revenue growth for FY27; the price implies about 3% a year earnings growth, if all profit became cash.
